Comparative Operating Systems Ablation & Audsley WCRT Verification

Mathematical Proof of Schedulability & Policy Benchmark

We benchmarked the 7-task surgical workload across three distinct kernel architectures and verified each task against **Audsley's Worst-Case Response Time (WCRT)** recurrence with non-preemptive atomic blocking factor $B_i$.

1. AEGIS-RTOS v6.0 (HYBRID + AGING) OPTIMAL

Zero Surgical Faults & Zero Starvation

  • • Arterial Incision Safety: `PID-103` holds the Atomic Lock at `T=4..6ms`, preventing `PID-104` from severing the femoral artery mid-cut.
  • • Emergency Response: `PID-104` (Code Red V-Fib) dispatches at `T=7ms` and finishes at `T=10ms` (within its `11ms` hard deadline).
  • • Starvation Immunity: `PID-101` (Base `P85`) ages `5x` (`P85` → `P12`) and completes at T=18ms (`30.8%` faster than without aging).
2. HYBRID WITHOUT AGING STARVATION RISK

Severe Telemetry Starvation (`T=26ms`)

  • • What Happens: Without dynamic aging, `PID-101` remains stuck at `P85` while `PID-102` (`P55`), `PID-105` (`P38`), `PID-106` (`P32`), and `PID-107` (`P4`) continually execute ahead of it.
  • • Deadline Failure: `PID-101` is starved until the very end of the horizon (T=26ms, waiting `20ms` vs `12ms`), violating its `22ms` telemetry deadline!
3. PURE PREEMPTIVE (NO ATOMIC LOCK) FATAL HAZARD

Mid-Incision Actuator Interruption

  • • What Happens: At `T=4ms`, `PID-104` (`P1`) forcibly preempts `PID-103` (`P22`) while the `450mW` surgical laser is actively cutting the femoral artery (`2/5ms` progress).
  • • Clinical Consequence: Leaving an unsealed arterial laser incision open during high-voltage defibrillation causes catastrophic hemorrhage.

Silicon & Operating System Architecture

AEGIS-RTOS v6.0 APEX Formal Kernel Specification

1. Mathematical Formulation of Scheduler, WCRT & Aging

Let $\mathcal{Q}_{\text{ready}}(t)$ denote the set of ready tasks at millisecond tick $t$. Each task $T_i$ maintains a static base priority $P_i^{\text{base}} \in [1, 99]$, a dynamic effective priority $P_i^{\text{eff}}(t)$, a current ready-queue wait counter $w_i(t)$, an aging period $\tau_i$, an aging decrement $\Delta_i$, and a priority ceiling floor $P_i^{\text{floor}}$:

P_i^eff(t + 1) = max( P_i^floor, P_i^eff(t) - Δ_i ) if w_i(t) > 0 and w_i(t) mod τ_i == 0
T_cand(t) = argmin_{T_i in Q_ready(t)} ( P_i^eff(t), -w_i(t), A_i, PID_i )
B_i = max_{k : P_k > P_i and is_atomic(k)} ( C_k - 1 )
R_i = C_i + B_i + sum_{j in hp(i)} ceil( R_i / T_j ) * C_j <= D_i

By bounding aging promotions at $P_i^{\text{floor}} \in [12, 18]$ for background and diagnostic tasks, the scheduler guarantees that starved tasks smoothly overtake incoming medium-priority tasks (`P20`–`P55`) while never blocking `P1`–`P10` life-support routines.
